tasks.short: Prepare lecture content with images, recordings and scores, deliver lectures and demonstrations, check the rights of media used, publish slides and recordings, and answer questions after class.

steps.what: Arts teacher prepares lectures, selecting images, recordings and scores
Arts teacher delivers lectures to students on acting techniques, fundamentals of music or art history
Arts teacher checks the rights of images and recordings before sharing them
Arts teacher uploads slides and recordings for students
Arts teacher answers students' questions after the lecture

tasks.design: Images, recordings and scores come from the library's licensed collections in a shared media library ({DOCS}) that shows the rights per item, so the teacher reuses and checks less. Once the teacher has checked the rights, slides and recordings are published to the course in the learning environment ({LMS}). Lecturing, demonstrating and answering questions stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Media were searched for each lecture and rights checked one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Library media collections show licence terms per item.
tasks.still_hard: Many works outside the collections still need a rights check.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a student how a phrase should breathe.

reach.learn: Whether teachers find what they need in the collections.

evidence.claim: Library media collections can show licence terms per image or recording.

assumptions: Boundary: from the course plan to questions answered; assessment is outside.
Input contract: media from library collections; fallback is searching and checking rights by hand.
research_questions: How much media comes from the licensed collections?

incremental.description: Arts teacher requests missing works from the library.

approvals.approved_version: The slides and recordings as rights-checked by the teacher in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: much media from outside the collections; high: mostly licensed collection items.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write the syllabus, write homework assignments, prepare handouts and reading lists, check the materials together, publish them to students, and print handouts.

steps.what: Arts teacher prepares the course syllabus

loop.input: The course catalogue entry with learning outcomes and credits, the academic calendar and last year's syllabus.
loop.output: A draft syllabus with fixed fields filled and weekly descriptions drafted.
loop.check: Code checks every learning outcome from the catalogue appears, dates match the academic calendar and credits match; the teacher edits and approves the text.
loop.stop: Stops when the checks pass and the teacher approves, or after two failed redrafts the teacher writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Weekly descriptions need prose; a template fills only the fixed fields.

steps.what: Arts teacher writes homework assignments
Arts teacher prepares handouts and reading lists
Arts teacher checks the course materials together
Arts teacher uploads the materials for students
Arts teacher prints and copies handouts

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts the syllabus from the course catalogue entry, the academic calendar and last year's syllabus; code checks outcomes, dates and credits, and the teacher edits the weekly text. Assignments and handouts are kept in a shared course library ({DOCS}) for reuse, and reading lists link to the library catalogue so each item resolves. Once the teacher has checked everything, the materials are published in the learning environment ({LMS}) and handouts are no longer printed. Writing the assignments stays with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Syllabi were retyped each year and handouts copied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft syllabi from catalogue data; learning environments replace printed handouts.
tasks.still_hard: Creative assignments need to be new each year to avoid copying.
tasks.human_edge: Setting an assignment that pushes a student just past their comfort.
tasks.altitude: The teacher checks and edits drafts instead of retyping.

reach.learn: Whether syllabi match the catalogue at first check.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft a syllabus from catalogue data and last year's text.
Drafting syllabi falls outside the Annex III education uses, which cover admission, evaluating learning outcomes and detecting cheating.

assumptions: Boundary: from the course catalogue entry to printed handouts; teaching is outside.
Input contract: catalogue entries from the programme office; academic calendar from the registrar; fallback is writing by hand.
Writing assignments stays with the teacher.
No student data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How much of the drafted syllabus does the teacher change?

already_counted.description: Arts teacher edits and approves the drafted syllabus.

incremental.description: Arts teacher keeps the shared course library tidy.

approvals.approved_version: The course materials as checked by the teacher in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new courses with no earlier materials; high: repeat courses with yearly updates.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Have students sign in, check attendance, type it into a spreadsheet, record grades, check final grades, enter them in student administration, and keep other required records.

steps.what: Students sign the paper attendance list
Arts teacher passes the list round and checks attendance in class
Arts teacher maintains student attendance records in a spreadsheet
Arts teacher records grades in the course gradebook
Arts teacher checks the final grades as examiner
Arts teacher types the grades into the student administration system
Arts teacher keeps other required records such as practice hours and jury results

tasks.design: Students check in by scanning a class code in the learning environment ({LMS}), so no paper list is passed round or retyped. Rubric scores flow into the gradebook, jury results and practice hours are kept in the same course record, and students see their own attendance and grades in the portal. Once the teacher has checked the final grades as examiner, they pass to the student administration system ({OTHER}) without retyping.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attendance was on paper, records in spreadsheets and grades typed into two systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning environments take check-ins by code and pass grades to student administration.
tasks.still_hard: Students can check in for a friend.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a student who stopped coming needs a call.
tasks.altitude: The teacher checks records instead of typing them.

reach.learn: Whether students check their records in the portal.

evidence.claim: At Radboud, grades entered in Brightspace must also be published in OSIRIS, a double entry.
Attendance and grades are personal data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the attendance list to other records kept; exam board decisions are outside.
Input contract: class lists from student administration; rubric scores from assessment; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.
Students scan a code in about the time it took to sign the list, and look up their records in the portal; priced as customer time.
Checking final grades stays with the teacher as examiner.

incremental.description: Arts teacher corrects check-ins made on behalf of others.
Students scan the class code and look up their records in the portal.

approvals.approved_version: The final grades as checked by the teacher in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small studio classes with few records; high: large classes with many records.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Scan current literature, read the important pieces, talk with colleagues, choose and register for conferences, attend them, and keep notes and references.

steps.what: Arts teacher searches and scans current literature in the field

loop.input: Library database alerts on the teacher's topics and the papers they point to.
loop.output: Short topic summaries, each sentence linked to a paper.
loop.check: Code checks every linked paper resolves in the library catalogue or by DOI, else the sentence is dropped; the teacher decides what to read.
loop.stop: Stops after one summary per alert; topics with no resolving papers are shown as titles only.
loop.why_not_simpler: Alerts list titles only; judging relevance from titles still takes the teacher's reading time.

steps.what: Arts teacher reads selected current literature
Arts teacher keeps abreast of developments by talking with colleagues
Arts teacher chooses which conferences and festivals to attend
Arts teacher registers for the chosen events online
Arts teacher participates in professional conferences and festivals
Arts teacher keeps notes and references from reading and conferences

tasks.design: Library database alerts on the teacher's topics feed a bounded summary step: each sentence links to a paper, and code drops any sentence whose paper does not resolve in the catalogue or by DOI. The teacher decides what to read in full. References are imported by DOI into a reference manager with notes. Reading, talking with colleagues and attending events stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Journals and alerts were scanned title by title.
tasks.enabler_now: Research tools summarise topics with linked papers; reference managers import by DOI.
tasks.still_hard: Much in the arts is learned at performances and exhibitions, not from papers.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a new staging at a festival and bringing it to class.
tasks.altitude: The teacher reads what matters instead of scanning everything.

reach.learn: Whether summaries point to papers teachers read.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and points to foundational papers.

assumptions: Boundary: from research interests to reference notes; publishing research is outside.
Input contract: alerts from the library's databases; fallback is scanning journals.
Reading, talking and attending do not change.
Registration fees are approved as today.
research_questions: Does the teacher read more relevant papers?

already_counted.description: Arts teacher reads summaries to choose papers.

incremental.description: Arts teacher tunes alert topics with the librarian.

approvals.approved_version: The events as chosen by the teacher in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a field followed mostly through performances; high: a field with much written research.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The arts teacher keeps lecturing, setting assignments, judging grades and learning from the field; searching media, retyping syllabi, paper lists and scanning titles shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends saved time in the studio with students.
